draft.title: Kinds of evidence from the ancient past
card: Historians and archaeologists study sources, which are the things that give us clues about the past. Ancient sources include art, symbols, writing, tools, buildings, human remains and oral traditions.

Writing, such as letters, laws and records on clay tablets, can tell us what people thought and did. Oral traditions are stories, songs and knowledge passed down by speaking from one generation to the next.
Tools, buildings, art and human remains show how people lived, worked and died. They cannot tell us what people thought unless we also have other sources.
Every kind of source has strengths and gaps. Many things rot away or are lost, so no single source gives the whole story. Historians compare different kinds of evidence to build a fuller picture.
draft.remember: Each kind of evidence has strengths and gaps, so historians use several kinds together.

a.q: Why do historians compare several kinds of evidence about an ancient society?
opts: Each kind has gaps that others may help to fill
Only one kind of evidence can ever be correct
Written sources are always more truthful than objects
Objects show what people thought better than writing
a.why: Each source shows only part of the past, so using several kinds gives a fuller picture. It is wrong to say writing is always more truthful, because the card says every kind has strengths and gaps.
a.clue: Think about what is left out of any one source.

b.q: Archaeologists dig up the stone foundations of a house and some tools in an ancient village. What can this evidence show, and what is a gap?
opts: It shows how people lived, but not what they thought
It shows what people thought, but not how they lived
It shows how people lived, and nothing is left out
It shows nothing, as only writing counts as evidence
b.why: Buildings and tools show how people lived and worked. On their own they cannot tell us what people thought, so that is a gap. Saying they show what people thought reverses the strength and the gap.
b.clue: Objects and buildings show actions more than ideas.

a.best: Each kind has gaps that others may help to fill

b.best: It shows how people lived, but not what they thought

problems.detail: The card says tools, buildings, art and human remains 'cannot tell us what people thought' without other sources. Art, symbols and burials (such as grave goods) are often key evidence for ancient beliefs, even with no writing. Grouping art here and saying 'cannot' is misleading. Something like 'can tell us less about what people thought' would be accurate.
The clue 'Objects and buildings show actions more than ideas' restates the right option almost directly, so a student can pick it without thinking about the evidence.

check.summary: Both questions have one clearly right answer, but the card overstates its point: it says art and other objects cannot tell us what people thought, when art and burials are often used as evidence of beliefs. The clue for question b also nearly gives the answer away.
